evidence.detail: Only rs/l/d/c LoginScreen references rs/l/d/a; LoginScreen allocates and owns the complete live list of these objects.
LoginScreen seeds the presentation using exact asset 'orb 1', while rs/l/d/a loads randomized exact 'orb N' sprite variants from /assets/.
LoginScreen constructs 75 rs/l/d/a instances during initialization and iterates the same list throughout login rendering/input updates.

Each object owns one selected orb sprite plus position/fixed-point movement state, randomized movement mode, return-to-origin state and hit/attraction behavior; its update method ends by rendering that orb sprite at its current login-screen position.
No class outside LoginScreen consumes rs/l/d/a, so the orb role is confined to LoginScreen presentation rather than a reusable game-world particle/entity subsystem.

candidates.note: LoginOrb is descriptive exact-behavior recovery for one animated orb in the LoginScreen-owned 75-orb presentation swarm. The 'orb N' asset family survives exactly; confidence is 0.998.

evidence.detail: Only rs/l/d/c LoginScreen references or constructs rs/l/d/b; no second client subsystem consumes the class.
LoginScreen loads the exact /assets/messagebox sprite and passes that sprite into every rs/l/d/b construction.
The class stores exactly two message Strings and renders both over the supplied messagebox sprite using LoginScreen/Client fonts, with mutable position, visibility and alpha state.

LoginScreen uses one persistent instance for exact recovery/PIN guidance ('It will be your account\'s PIN before October 2024' / 'If you do not remember it, request help on our forums!') and creates additional instances from dynamic login-message pairs.

The class implements fade-in/reset, active-state queries, alternate centered/left text layout and position setters, matching a LoginScreen message box rather than a domain model or generic network message.

candidates.note: LoginMessageBox is descriptive exact-behavior recovery for LoginScreen's exclusive two-line messagebox renderer. Exact asset ownership and message usage support confidence 0.998.
